html:
Table. Table 1 from prop:substrate-consistency-window

Determination Observable q value Source
Lepton mass ratio m_\mu / m_e \approx 206.7682830 1.10997 \pm 0.001 CODATA 2018
Electromagnetic coupling \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}^{-1} \approx 137.036 1.11023 \pm 0.00002 CODATA 2022
Tritium half-life t_{1/2}({}^3\mathrm{H}) \sim 1.109--1.112 PDG

The q value is unchanged by the CODATA vintage. Inverting the bare form \alpha^{-1}_{\mathrm{bare}} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q for the 2018 and 2022 central values (137.035999084, 137.035999177) gives 1.11023043771 and 1.11023043782 — a shift of 1.1 \times 10^{-10}, five orders of magnitude below the \pm 0.00002 quoted. Only the source label moved.

These are the electromagnetic determination of q, not the substrate anchor q_0 = 1.10997858\ldots; the bare form gives 136.8232 at q_0, and the gap to the measured 137.036 is the Chern–Simons dressing (fine-structure data). Both figures and the shift are reproduced at 40 dps in substrate_consistency_window_q_from_alpha_em_probe.py, which also measures the ratio as 1.82\times10^{5} — the "six orders" above was an overstatement and is corrected here; the conclusion it supports is unaffected.
